text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - Thai oil crushers bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for January shipment, Settasan Settakarun of the Thai Cottonseed, Ricebran and Vegetable Oil Crushers Association said. The tender was settled at around $291-$295 a tonne C&F Bangkok and Louis Dreyfus was the supplier.

SUNFLOWERSEED OIL SALE - India contracted to import about 50,000 tonnes of sunflowerseed oil from the United States for shipment in December and January, Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, said on Tuesday.

VEGOIL TENDER - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation said on Tuesday it was unable to buy 7,000 tonnes of cottonseed meal and 7,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal as there were no offers.

BARLEY TENDER - Saudi Arabia is in the market to import 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley for January delivery, European grain traders said. The exact date of the tender was not immediately available but traders said Saudi Arabia was likely to tender on Tuesday or Wednesday.
CORN TENDER - Tunisia launched a tender for the purchase on Wednesday of two lots of corn of 25,000 tonnes each, traders said. Shipment dates are Jan 1-10 and Jan 20-31 1997.

SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company invited bids for up to 50,000 tonnes of soybeans for loading by Dec 20 and delivery by Jan 15. The company has asked traders to send separate bids, one for 30,000 tonnes and one for 50,000 tonnes, both as single cargoes and is expected to select only one cargo. The soybeans could be any origin. Another trader said the company asked for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, No. 2 or better. Food Industries Company was not available to clarify.

WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan issued separate tenders on Saturday for 225,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat and Australian white milling wheat for delivery between December 11 and 31, the Food and Agriculture Ministry said. The ministry invited bids on December 1.

- Sri Lanka will buy 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat on Wednesday, an official for the Co-operative Wholesale Establishment said. The tender will close on Wednesday . The tender is for 50,000 tonnes of soft white wheat slated for last half Dec delivery and another 50,000 tonnes of hard red and/or spring wheat for delivery during the first half of January.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Bangladesh has tendered for 200,000 tonnes of U.S. grade 2 wheat for shipment in January and February, food ministry officials said. They said the ministry would receive offers until 0600 GMT on November 30. The shipment for the first 100,000 tonnes should be completed by January 10 and the rest by February 10. The results of the bids will not be known until Dec 3 when a cabinet meeting decides on the offers.

- Algeria is expected this Friday to seek 100,000 tonnes optional origin wheat which would include French, U.S. or Argentine wheat, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for last-half Dec. The class of wheat was not given, they said.

LENTIL TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as final date for bids and results would be announced on December 17.

MARKET TALK - Russia will largely be able to meet its wheat needs this year, but grain is of low quality and Russia's Far East may continue imports as in recent years, a bread inspection official said on Tuesday.
